# cancho-cache

> A Redis-compatible cache written in cancho: strings and hashes, expiry and an LRU eviction policy over RESP2 and RESP3, on one thread with a fixed arena (sized at start, nothing allocated afterwards). No Ffi and no unsafe; its authority report names the one file it reads (/dev/urandom, for the hash seed) and no foreign code. Alpha: a string-and-hash cache, not a Redis replacement.

## Use it
- [Quick start](https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho-cache#quick-start): build the compiler at the pinned revision, build the cache, talk to it with redis-cli.
- [Commands](https://github.com/alpibrusl/cancho-cache#commands): 69 of Redis 7.0's 240 (strings, hashes, expiry, keyspace, transactions); every reply is byte-identical to Redis 7.0.15 for the cases in tests/differential.py.

## Facts that matter when calling it
- Clients tested: redis-cli, redis-py (RESP2, RESP3, default), ioredis, node-redis and redis-rs; the matrix is checked against the README in CI. Transactions work (MULTI, EXEC, DISCARD, WATCH, UNWATCH), so redis-py's default pipeline() and ioredis's multi().exec() work; WATCH follows up to eight keys and EXEC may abort when an unrelated key shares a bucket with a watched one.
- Limits (fixed): one database, 256 connections, a 16 KiB command. CONFIG SET is refused; settings are fixed at start.
- Not implemented: lists, sets and sorted sets, pub/sub, scripting, persistence, replication, cluster, TLS.
- Memory full: noeviction answers Redis's own -OOM error; allkeys-lru evicts.

## Optional
